privacy.ai_training_note: Official privacy policy states: 'We do not use your Personal Data to train and/or create separate artificial intelligence/products.' However, Lensa does train custom per-user models on uploaded face data to generate personalized Magic Avatars and effects; these custom models are not retained after generation. Historical reports and external sources (2022-2023) suggested broader data use for model training, but current official policy explicitly prohibits this. Photos for Magic Avatars are deleted immediately after generation; Art Styles photos retained max 24 hours on AWS; AI-Assistant features use OpenAI which retains photos up to 30 days.
privacy.data_region: United States (AWS, Google Cloud). Standard Contractual Clauses for EEA/UK data transfers.

security.name: Data Protection
security.value: Lensa employs 'reasonable and appropriate information security safeguards' but acknowledges limitations: 'we cannot guarantee the security of the collected information transmitted to or through Lensa.' The company notes 'there is no ideal technology or measure to maintain 100% security.'

security.name: Encryption Standards
security.value: No specific encryption protocols or standards (TLS versions, AES encryption, etc.) are documented in the public privacy policy or terms of service.

security.name: Third-Party Data Processing
security.value: User data shared with affiliates (Palta companies in Cyprus), AWS, Google Cloud Platform, Firebase, AppsFlyer, Amplitude, and OpenAI (for AI-Assistant features). Data may be disclosed during mergers or in response to legal requests.

security.name: Data Breach Notification
security.value: Lensa commits to 'informing you of such security incident in accordance with our Privacy Policy' when data loss occurs outside their control.

security.name: Third-Party Security Audits
security.value: No public security audit reports, penetration testing results, or third-party security certifications found on vendor-domain sources.

products.name: Lensa Photo Editor (Mobile App)
products.data_scope: User uploads photos/videos; processes via cloud (AWS, GCP); generates AI effects (Magic Avatars, Art Styles, portrait retouching, background blur/replacement); deletes originals per retention policy.
products.notes: Primary product. Processes biometric data (facial geometry) via Apple's TrueDepth API. Trains temporary per-user models for avatar/effect generation only. Available on iOS and Android.

compare.pricing_model: Freemium (free app with in-app purchases for credits and subscriptions). Virtual item purchases are 'final and non-refundable.'
compare.data_residency: United States (AWS, Google Cloud), with Standard Contractual Clauses for EEA/UK compliance.

flags: Despite processing biometric data (facial geometry), Lensa holds no public SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 27017, or ISO 27018 certifications. This is unusual for a company handling sensitive personal data.

The Better Business Bureau rates Prisma Labs, Inc. as 'F' due to failure to respond to 2 filed complaints. The BBB file opened 12/5/2022; the business started 5/15/2016. This raises questions about responsiveness to compliance issues.

There is an apparent contradiction around AI training: the official privacy policy states 'We do not use your Personal Data to train separate AI products,' but historical reports (ArtNews, ArtMajeur, 2022-2023) and earlier ToS language suggest Lensa previously used user data for AI model training. The current policy appears to narrowly exclude per-user custom model training (used only for that user's avatars and effects) from the definition of 'training separate products.' Buyers should ask the vendor to clarify this ambiguity.

Lensa's data security posture is weak: the privacy policy explicitly states Lensa 'cannot guarantee the security' and 'there is no ideal technology or measure to maintain 100% security.' This low-assurance language is concerning for a vendor processing biometric and facial data.
The public privacy policy and terms do not specify encryption standards, protocols, or key management practices for data in transit or at rest.
Lensa does not publish a trust center, security documentation, or compliance audit reports on its vendor domain.

Lensa collects facial geometry (via Apple TrueDepth) and other biometric data without formal security certifications or third-party audits. A lawsuit under the Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act (BIPA) has been filed alleging collection of facial geometry without proper consent.

Lensa's underlying Magic Avatars and Art Styles models use third-party models (Stable Diffusion) trained on internet images with unclear licensing. While this does not directly implicate Lensa's data handling, it raises questions about IP governance and vendor oversight of third-party dependencies.

Data retention policies vary by feature: 24 hours for Art Styles, immediate for Magic Avatars, and 30 days for the AI-Assistant via OpenAI. There is no global data retention policy, and the multi-vendor data lifecycle is complex.

Lensa claims GDPR compliance via Standard Contractual Clauses but provides no formal evaluation letter, no Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA), and no auditor confirmation of the adequacy of its safeguards.
